newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Ortega offers to negotiate seized Nicaraguan home.
newsitem.headline: Ortega offers to negotiate seized Nicaraguan home.

text.p: Nicaraguan President Arnoldo Aleman on Friday praised his bitter rival, Sandinista leader Daniel Ortega, who offered to discuss a settlement on a house Ortega confiscated.
"I recognise the merit of Commander Ortega, who said that the personal case (of his house) should not be excluded from the negotiations on private property," Aleman told reporters.
Ortega, who led the 1979-1990 left-wing Sandinista government that confiscated private property, lives in a house that was confiscated from the family of Aleman's chief adviser, Jaime Morales Carazo.

Ortega's refusal to return the house to Morales or pay its market value had become a major sticking point in relations between Aleman's Liberal Alliance and the Sandinistas, Nicaragua's two dominant political forces.
Aleman has long insisted that Ortega pay for the house or get out, a suggestion Ortega refused to discuss until now.
Aleman said he met Ortega on Thursday and Ortega told him he was "totally open" to negotiating ownership of the house and had "no interest" in a house not acquired legally.
Ortega even offered to open up the street in front of the house to traffic and remove the soldiers who guarded it, another longtime complaint of the Liberals, Aleman said.
Ortega was not available for comment.
An elated Aleman said that with Ortega's offer Nicaragua was well on its way to resolving its lingering private property problem, which had scared off foreign investment.
Despite the return of the free market to Nicaragua in 1990, thousands of conflicts remain between people who received confiscated property in the 1980s and the former owners, who want it back.
